question.problem:
Given that a positive geometric sequence has 
${a}_{3}=12$, ${a}_{5}=3$ and ${a}_{k}=48$, what is the value of $k?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the common ratio. We are told that ${a}_{3}=12$ and ${a}_{5}=3,$ so we can find the common ratio using a formula, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{n-m} & =\frac{{a}_{n}}{{a}_{m}} \\ {r}^{5-3} & =\frac{{a}_{5}}{{a}_{3}} \\ {r}^{5-3} & =\frac{3}{12} \\ {r}^{2} & =\frac{1}{4} \\ {r}^{2} & ={(\frac{1}{2})}^{2} \\ r & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We disregard the negative solution since we are told that the sequence is positive.

Now that we know the common ratio is $r=\frac{1}{2}$, we can use the same formula to solve for the value of $k$ such that ${a}_{k}=48:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{n-m} & =\frac{{a}_{n}}{{a}_{m}} \\ {r}^{k-3} & =\frac{{a}_{k}}{{a}_{3}} \\ {(\frac{1}{2})}^{k-3} & =\frac{48}{12} \\ {(\frac{1}{2})}^{k-3} & =4 \\ {(\frac{1}{2})}^{k-3} & ={(\frac{1}{2})}^{-2} \\ k-3 & =-2 \\ k & =1\end{aligned}
$$
